item.title: Perioperative immunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Hörner M, Hartmann S, Adkins DR, Uppaluri R
item.description:
Authors: Hörner M, Hartmann S, Adkins DR, Uppaluri R
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70642
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42844879



Abstract:
Outcomes for patients with resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remain suboptimal despite multimodal therapy, with high rates of recurrence and patients suffering from toxicity of treatments. Immune checkpoint inhibitors, which have transformed the management of recurrent and metastatic disease, have been advanced into the perioperative and adjuvant settings. Recent phase III trials mark a turning point: the addition of adjuvant nivolumab improved disease-free survival in pathologic high-risk resected HNSCCs, while perioperative pembrolizumab significantly prolonged event-free survival in resectable locally advanced HNSCCs, supporting a shift toward integrated perioperative immunotherapy strategies. Although the former approach fits into a conventional adjuvant framework, biological insights suggest that neoadjuvant delivery enables effective immune priming extending therapeutic approaches. Together, these advances redefine therapeutic strategies in resectable HNSCC and highlight the potential of perioperative immunotherapy to improve long-term outcomes.

item.title: Oral and Fecal Microbial Dysbiosis as Non-Invasive Diagnostic Biomarkers for Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70779
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42865226



Abstract:
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.846 (95% CI: 0.824-0.867), though with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%). By cancer type, pooled AUCs were 0.746 for EC (5 cohorts), 0.886 for GC (8 cohorts), and 0.850 for CRC (46 cohorts). A bivariate analysis of 20 cohorts comparing sample types found no statistically significant difference in diagnostic performance between oral (sAUC = 0.863) and fecal sampling (sAUC = 0.820; p = 0.369). While these exploratory findings suggest that oral and fecal microbial biomarkers may offer comparable diagnostic accuracy for GI cancers, with oral sampling presenting a more practical option for screening, the results are preliminary. Significant heterogeneity, a limited number of oral cohorts, and the absence of clinical control groups highlight the need for large-scale prospective studies with direct comparisons and real-world validation to validate these biomarkers for clinical translation.

item.title: Familial Cancers Associated With Cancers of the Breast, Prostate, Colorectum, and Lung in Sweden.
item.dc:creator: Zitricky F, Sundquist K, Sundquist J, Hemminki A, Försti A, Hemminki K
item.description:
Authors: Zitricky F, Sundquist K, Sundquist J, Hemminki A, Försti A, Hemminki K
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70781
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42865221



Abstract:
Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

item.title: Efficacy of Physical Therapy on Maximal Mouth Opening in Patients Affected by Disc Displacement and Degenerative Temporomandibular Joint Diseases: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Ferrillo M, De Rosa A, Quinzi V, Conte C, Francica A, Ammendolia A, Giudice A, de Sire A
item.description:
Authors: Ferrillo M, De Rosa A, Quinzi V, Conte C, Francica A, Ammendolia A, Giudice A, de Sire A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70517
Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 42864746



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among temporomandibular disorders (TMDs), the main arthrogenic entities are disc-condylar complex disorders and degenerative diseases. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy in patients with temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science until January 2026 to search for studies including patients with a diagnosis of intracapsular TMD as participants; physical therapy or physical therapy combined to other conservative approaches as intervention; placebo, sham treatments, oral pharmacological anti-inflammatory drugs, behavioral therapy, or other conservative approaches as comparison; maximal mouth opening (MMO) as outcome. RESULTS: Out of 1578 identified records, 10 studies were included. A total of 354 subjects were analyzed, of which 213 performed a rehabilitation technique and 141 were included in the control group. Although the randomized trials reported improvement in MMO, pain, and function, a major limitation was the lack of standardized physiotherapy protocols across trials. CONCLUSION: Findings from the present systematic review showed that physiotherapy (active and passive jaw exercises, associated with relaxation techniques) might improve MMO. Further studies with uniform protocols and high-quality randomized trials are needed to validate the efficacy of multimodal treatments in arthrogenic TMD subtypes.

item.title: Hitting KRAS G12D without the gut punch: Can immunotherapy make it last?
item.dc:creator: Kim DW, Garrido-Laguna I
item.description:
Authors: Kim DW, Garrido-Laguna I
Journal: Cancer cell | DOI: 10.1016/j.ccell.2026.09.009
Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 42863460



Abstract:
In this issue of Cancer Cell, Shi et al. report encouraging early-phase results combining HRS-4642, an allele-specific KRAS G12D inhibitor, with the PD-L1 inhibitor adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer. The intravenous combination was safe and well tolerated, notably sparing patients the gastrointestinal toxicity common to oral KRAS inhibitors, and achieved a promising 43% response rate at the recommended dose.

item.title: Socioeconomic and clinical factors associated with odontogenic infection types among hospitalised patients in Periurban Ghana.
item.dc:creator: Okyere Boadu KA, Asante LS, Frimpong P, Johnson EK, Adu VW, Okyere Boadu R
item.description:
Authors: Okyere Boadu KA, Asante LS, Frimpong P, Johnson EK, Adu VW, Okyere Boadu R
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360737
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42862874



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Odontogenic infections may progress to life-threatening complications if not managed promptly, and socioeconomic circumstances have been linked to their presentation, particularly where access to dental care is limited. Because every patient studied was already hospitalised, this analysis addresses the clinical type of infection at presentation, not the risk of developing one. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cross-sectional review of hospital records was undertaken at the Allied Ward of Sunyani Teaching Hospital (January 2021 to January 2025). Of 811 consecutive admissions, 525 were excluded: 509 for non-odontogenic conditions and 16 for records missing more than 30% of required clinical fields, leaving 286 complete records. Chi-square tests were reported with Cramer's V and Monte Carlo exact p-values where cells were sparse. Because the unpenalised model showed quasi-complete separation, the primary analysis was a Firth-penalised multinomial logistic regression, with abscess as the reference outcome. RESULTS: Adjusting for age, sex, employment, residence, recorded oral hygiene, systemic comorbidity and alcohol use, unemployment was associated with higher adjusted odds of Ludwig's angina (LA) and not abscess (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.27-6.09), and rural residence with necrotizing fasciitis (NF; AOR = 3.62, 95% CI 1.33-9.80). Systemic comorbidity was associated with LA (AOR = 4.14, 95% CI 1.83-9.36), NF (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI 2.95-25.75) and cellulitis (AOR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.03-4.18). Absence of a recorded poor-hygiene entry was associated with cellulitis (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI 2.42-26.83), interpreted as a documentation artefact not a protective effect. Sex and alcohol use showed no association. Number of children, the sole source of separation, was not retained; its penalised intervals included 1. CONCLUSION: Unemployment and systemic comorbidity were associated with more severe presentations, and rural residence with NF specifically. Findings are associational and describe variation in infection type among admitted patients rather than infection risk, within a retrospective single-centre design.

item.title: Effects of Isthmus-Sparing Lobectomy on Thyroid Function: A Prospective, Multicenter, Comparative Study.
item.dc:creator: Kim WW, Jeon YS, Cho J, Lee JH, Youn HJ, Kang SH, Choi JE, Jeong YJ, Bae D, Lee MH, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Kim WW, Jeon YS, Cho J, Lee JH, Youn HJ, Kang SH, Choi JE, Jeong YJ, Bae D, Lee MH, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70510
Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 42861680



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prospective study evaluated the impact of isthmus management (isthmus-sparing vs. isthmus-removing lobectomy) on postoperative hypothyroidism risk. METHODS: Between January 2022 and March 2023, 326 euthyroid patients with benign or low-risk papillary thyroid cancer were randomized into the isthmus-sparing (IS, n = 164) or isthmus-removing (IR, n = 162) group. Administration of levothyroxine was limited to patients with overt hypothyroidism or symptomatic subclinical hypothyroidism. RESULTS: TSH levels were significantly lower in the IS group at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months ( p < 0.05 ). Euthyroidism maintenance was higher in the IS group (62.2% vs. 38.9%, p = 0.001 ). The IS group showed lower subclinical hypothyroidism (33.8% vs. 54.9%, p = 0.001 ) and hormone replacement rates (8.5% vs. 25.3%, p = 0.001 ). Overt hypothyroidism was lower in the IS group without statistical significance (6.1% vs. 12.3%, p = 0.057 ). CONCLUSION: Isthmus-sparing lobectomy better preserves thyroid function and reduces postoperative subclinical hypothyroidism and hormone replacement needs compared to isthmus-removing lobectomy.

item.title: Effects of Antimicrobial Mouthwashes on Oral Health and Blood Pressure: A Preliminary Parallel Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.dc:creator: Bhowmick D, Nayek M, Aquil A, Rudra A, Mistry S, Nair V, Das I
item.description:
Authors: Bhowmick D, Nayek M, Aquil A, Rudra A, Mistry S, Nair V, Das I
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70537
Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 42861455



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although antimicrobial mouthwashes vary in efficacy and safety for managing biofilm-induced gingivitis, concerns remain regarding their potential to reduce nitric oxide bioavailability and increase hypertension risk. Therefore, we investigated whether octenidine is more effective and causes fewer adverse events than chlorhexidine, and whether antimicrobial mouthwash use increases hypertension risk. METHODS: In this parallel randomized controlled trial, 90 participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to rinse with 10 mL of 2% saline (Group I), 0.2% chlorhexidine (Group II), or 0.1% octenidine (Group III) for 21 days. Co-primary outcomes (clinical parameters and blood pressure) and secondary outcomes (salivary bacterial count, adverse events, and pulse pressure) were assessed over 42 days. RESULTS: At day 22, antimicrobial mouthwashes significantly reduced clinical (29%-52%) and microbial (> 92%) measures (p < 0.001), whereas saline produced minimal changes (p > 0.05). Salivary nitrate levels showed the opposite trend. Groups II and III showed comparable efficacy, but octenidine was associated with fewer adverse events. Although systolic blood pressure increased slightly in all groups, the changes were clinically insignificant. Elevated pulse pressure in antimicrobial groups returned to baseline by Day 42. CONCLUSIONS: Octenidine (0.1%) was safer and comparably effective to chlorhexidine. Short-term antimicrobial mouthwash had no clinically significant effect on blood pressure. TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2024/08/072091 (India), date: 07/08/2024. URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTEwOTY5&Enc.

item.title: Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction in Hypermobile Patients.
item.dc:creator: Menton SM, Fairweather D, Wilson FC, Zangerle DJ, Murphy EF, Darakjian AA, Thompson CC, Gajarawala SN, Knight DRT, Bruno KA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Menton SM, Fairweather D, Wilson FC, Zangerle DJ, Murphy EF, Darakjian AA, Thompson CC, Gajarawala SN, Knight DRT, Bruno KA, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70980
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860825



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) or hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO) have more voice, cough, swallowing, GI issues, and MC activation than patients without ILO. METHODS: This retrospective study of 2162 patients meeting 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS (n = 507) or HSD (n = 1655) who were seen at the EDS Clinic in Mayo Clinic Florida from November 2019 to June 2025 compared patients who screened positive for ILO to those who screened negative. Patients were examined for self-reported symptoms of voice, cough, swallow, and GI issues as well as MC activation. RESULTS: Among patients with hEDS or HSD, 23.1% and 17.1% respectively screened positive for ILO. Patients with ILO had significantly more voice, cough, and swallow issues than patients without ILO (all p ≤ 0.007). Both diagnoses had more gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) (hEDS: 55.6% vs. 40.9%, p = 0.004; HSD: 55.8% vs. 42.2%, p < 0.0001). Additionally, both hEDS and HSD patients with ILO self-reported 18 allergy-related symptoms more often than those without ILO and had higher MC scores indicating widespread MC activation (all p < 0.0001). Cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC score were statistically significant predictors of ILO in both hEDS and HSD within a logistic regression analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC symptom burden were the strongest independent predictors of ILO across both hEDS and HSD, underscoring the need for routine multidisciplinary laryngeal assessment in this population.

item.title: Trajectories of Plasma Epstein-Barr Virus DNA and Clinical Outcomes in Recurrent or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Treated With PD-L1 Inhibitors: A Post-Hoc Analysis of a Multicenter, Phase II Study.
item.dc:creator: Pan Z, Pei Y, Diao J, Gao K, Ge J, Qing Y, Wei Y, Peng X
item.description:
Authors: Pan Z, Pei Y, Diao J, Gao K, Ge J, Qing Y, Wei Y, Peng X
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70473
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860770



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (R/M NPC) treated with immunotherapy remain limited. This study evaluated the association between longitudinal EBV DNA trajectories and clinical outcomes in patients with R/M NPC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from a multicenter, single-arm, Phase II trial evaluating the programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor KL-A167 in patients with previously treated R/M NPC. Plasma EBV DNA was measured at baseline and at each scheduled efficacy assessment, which was conducted every six weeks until disease progression. EBV DNA trajectories were distinguished through a logistic trajectory model. Multivariable Cox models were used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for survival outcomes. RESULTS: We identified three distinct trajectories: persistently undetectable (n = 17, 13.8%), fluctuating (n = 40, 32.5%), and persistently detectable (n = 66, 53.7%). Compared with the persistently undetectable group, HRs of death were 4.96 (95% CI, 1.60-15.40) and 12.59 (95% CI, 4.01-39.51) for the fluctuating and persistently detectable groups, respectively. HRs of disease progression were 1.96 (95% CI, 0.97-3.96) and 3.22 (95% CI, 1.56-6.67), respectively. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that plasma EBV DNA trajectories could be a promising biomarker for monitoring treatment response and longitudinal risk stratification.

item.title: CyberKnife Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy for Reirradiation of Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Outcomes and Prognostic Factors.
item.dc:creator: Sharon S, Qureshi MM, Keohan S, Luk S, Jang S, Truong MT
item.description:
Authors: Sharon S, Qureshi MM, Keohan S, Luk S, Jang S, Truong MT
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70494
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860746



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is used for reirradiation in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (RM-HNSCC), but prognostic factors remain unclear. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 36 RM-HNSCC patients treated with CyberKnife-SBRT (2009-2022). ENDPOINTS: local control (LC) and overall survival (OS), estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 8.5 months, median OS was 9.6 months, with 1- and 2-year OS rates of 43.5% and 34.2%. One- and 2-year LC rates were 55.1% and 34.5%, with median time-to-recurrence of 14.1 months. On multivariable analysis, smoking > 30 pack-years predicted worse LC (HR 5.68; 95% CI, 1.42-22.70; p = 0.014), while former/never smoking predicted improved OS (HR 0.26; 95% CI, 0.08-0.82; p = 0.022). Gross tumor volume > 37.0 cm3 predicted worse LC (log-rank p = 0.044) and OS (p = 0.003) on univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Smoking history independently predicted LC and OS; larger tumor volume was associated with worse outcomes and may inform patient selection for SBRT reirradiation.

item.title: Probe-Based Near-Infrared Autofluorescence for Parathyroid Identification During Thyroid Surgery: Clinical Outcomes, Surgeon Confidence, and Autofluorescence Thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Cheung AY, Wang B, Saito Y, Russell MD, Soffer JM, Okose OC, Trinh LN, Srikanthan A, Salem F, Sistovaris A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Cheung AY, Wang B, Saito Y, Russell MD, Soffer JM, Okose OC, Trinh LN, Srikanthan A, Salem F, Sistovaris A, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70503
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860718



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated experience with probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) system (PTeye) in parathyroid gland (PTG) identification during total thyroidectomy. METHODS: In this retrospective study, patients undergoing total thyroidectomy using PTeye (2020-2022; n = 84) were compared with a historical visual-identification cohort (2018-2019; n = 103). RESULTS: PTG identification rates were comparable, although 42% of PTGs detected with PTeye were initially visualized with low or moderate confidence. Significantly fewer patients in the PTeye cohort had PTGs incidentally identified on histology (4.8% vs. 16.5%, p = 0.018), but there was no difference in the incidence of autotransplanted PTGs or total inadvertent parathyroidectomy. Postoperative calcium was higher with PTeye (median 9.2 vs. 9.0 mg/dL, p < 0.001). Postoperative PTH, transient, and permanent hypoparathyroidism did not differ. An autofluorescence ratio cutoff of 2.5 improved specificity compared with the manufacturer-recommended cutoff of 1.2. CONCLUSIONS: PTeye provides adjunctive confirmation of suspected parathyroid tissue, including glands initially identified with low or moderate visual confidence.

item.title: Hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis enhances proliferation of oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
item.description:
Authors: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
Journal: British journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s41416-026-03632-6
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860443



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypoxic microenvironment, a common feature of solid tumors, is critically involved in driving cancer malignancy. This research focuses on elucidating the function of high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), induced by such hypoxia, in the context of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). METHODS: We first profiled HMGB1 expression patterns in clinical OSCC specimens and evaluated their potential associations with clinicopathological parameters. To functionally characterize HMGB1, we conducted in vitro experiments utilizing silencing strategies. The impact of chronic cyclic hypoxia and HMGB1 depletion on key cellular processes-including proliferation, pyroptosis, and cell cycle-was systematically examined in OSCC cells. Signaling activity along the HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 axis was determined by immunoblotting. Furthermore, in vivo relevance was substantiated through murine xenograft models and a 4-NQO-induced carcinogenesis protocol. RESULTS: Analysis of clinical samples revealed that HMGB1 is constitutively upregulated in OSCC tissues. This elevated expression demonstrated a positive relationship with both increased tumor dimensions and lymph node metastasis. Subsequent Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that heightened HMGB1 levels are a marker for unfavorable patient outcomes. Furthermore, in cell culture systems, hypoxia treatment significantly elevates HMGB1 expression levels in OSCC cells. Knockdown of HMGB1 expression inhibits hypoxia-induced NLRP3, cleaved-caspase-1, and HIF-1α expression. Hypoxia treatment markedly enhanced OSCC cell proliferation, induced pyroptosis, and alleviated G2/M phase arrest, while HMGB1 knockdown reversed the pro-tumor effects of hypoxia. In vivo experiments demonstrated that HMGB1 knockdown inhibited tumor growth, whereas NLRP3 or caspase-1 deficiency delayed oral cancer progression. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggested that HMGB1 contributes to the progression of OSCC and has prognostic value. Targeting the hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis may offer a viable therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ
item.description:
Authors: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111818
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858857



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

item.title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
item.dc:creator: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
item.description:
Authors: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111815
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858855



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy. METHODS AND MATERIALS: For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively. RESULTS: General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients. CONCLUSIONS: It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

item.title: Dose-effect analysis of late dental adverse effects following radiation therapy in survivors of paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma.
item.dc:creator: Krommenhoek KB, Hol MLF, van der Aa N, Suttie M, Gaze MN, Wiersma J, Mandeville HC, Gillies C, Slater O, Bel A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Krommenhoek KB, Hol MLF, van der Aa N, Suttie M, Gaze MN, Wiersma J, Mandeville HC, Gillies C, Slater O, Bel A, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111820
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858853



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcomas (HNRMS) often require radiotherapy, causing dental complications during critical development. Limited literature suggests dose-dependent risks, but clear thresholds for late dental adverse effects are lacking. This study aims to characterize dose effects on developing dentition in paediatric HNRMS patients to identify dose-response relationships informing evidence-based treatment planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Orthopantomograms from survivors of HNRMS were evaluated using the validated DENTALE scoring system. Radiation doses from brachytherapy, external beam radiation with protons and photons to deciduous teeth were retrieved from treatment plans and converted to EQD2 (α/β = 3 Gy). Dose-response relationships were modelled per tooth using binary logistic regression in Mplus (COMPLEX option for within-patient dependency; model fit assessed by ROC analysis). RESULTS: Among 34 survivors (median age at diagnosis 5.6 years), 27 (79.4 %) exhibited late dental AE. Of 919 assessable permanent teeth, 242 (26.3 %) showed abnormalities. Increasing radiation dose was consistently associated with higher AE probability. The dose corresponding to 50 % predicted probability of any dental AE was 23 Gy(EQD2). CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates dose-effect relationships for radiation exposure of developing dentition, with clinically relevant structure-specific thresholds. Teeth receiving no radiation still show developmental abnormalities, likely due to chemotherapy. item.title: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma prevention in high-risk, resource-limited rural China: Dysplasia screening and modifiable risk factors in a 14-year follow-up study.

item.description:
Authors: Pan D, Su M, Wang Y, Xu D, Han J, Wang X, Yan Q, Xu J, Wang N, Zhang Z, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103248
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858638



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality in resource-limited regions, where barriers to screening, unsafe environmental exposures, and constrained health infrastructure hinder timely diagnosis and survivorship. METHODS: We conducted a 14-year follow-up study involving 11,397 adults from a rural high-risk area of Huai'an, China, integrating baseline endoscopic biopsy, epidemiological assessment, and dietary evaluations. The Cox regression model was used to assess the hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). FDR was used to account for multiple testing. RESULTS: During follow-up, 189 incident ESCC cases were identified. Histological severity of dysplasia strongly predicted progression, particularly severe dysplasia (HR=16.22; 95% CI: 8.42-31.25) and carcinoma in situ (HR=52.90; 95% CI: 26.29-106.46). Male sex, increasing age, lower BMI (especially female smokers), a family history of ESCC, consumption of shallow well or surface water, and very spicy diets were significantly associated with increased ESCC risk. Frequent intake of banana (HR=0.54; 95% CI: 0.39-0.76; P-FDR=0.014) and hawthorn (HR=0.58; 95% CI: 0.42-0.81; P-FDR=0.023) was significantly associated with reduced ESCC risk. CONCLUSIONS: Histological severity of dysplasia is a strong predictor of ESCC development. In addition, compared with historical cohorts lacking organized early diagnosis and treatment, progression rates observed in this population suggest that the region's screening program may have contributed to improved outcomes. While early detection and treatment remain essential, modifying environmental and dietary exposures may provide additional avenues for prevention. The results support integrated prevention strategies that combine endoscopic screening with feasible lifestyle interventions to reduce ESCC burden in high-risk communities.

item.title: Invasive Cervical Cancers After an HPV-Negative Test: Insights From HPV Testing Histories.
item.dc:creator: Hassan SS, Nordqvist Kleppe S, Asinger N, Wang J, Dillner J, Arroyo Mühr LS
item.description:
Authors: Hassan SS, Nordqvist Kleppe S, Asinger N, Wang J, Dillner J, Arroyo Mühr LS
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70783
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42857941



Abstract:
Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is the primary method for cervical screening, and a negative HPV test is associated with a very low subsequent risk of invasive cancer. Nevertheless, some cervical cancers are diagnosed following an HPV-negative test. Using Swedish registry data, we identified women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer between 2019 and 2024 and reconstructed HPV testing histories from the National Cervical Screening Registry. The HPV test closest to diagnosis, performed before or within 30 days after diagnosis, was defined as the index test. Of 3000 women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer, 243 (8.1%) had an HPV-negative index test. These women were older and more frequently diagnosed at advanced stages than women with an HPV-positive index test. After adjustment for age, calendar year, and histology, an HPV-negative index test remained associated with advanced-stage disease (adjusted OR 2.91, 95% CI: 2.13-4.00). Among women with an HPV-negative index test, 128 of 243 (52.7%) had no prior HPV testing recorded, 83 of 243 (34.2%) had consistently HPV-negative histories, and 32 of 243 (13.2%) had prior HPV positivity. Cytology records were available for 229 to 243 (94.2%), and 33 to 243 (13.6%) had a previous high-grade histopathological diagnosis. Among women with an HPV-negative index test, recurrent HPV positivity following an intervening negative test was observed in only one woman. Cervical cancers diagnosed after an HPV-negative test reflect heterogeneous HPV testing histories. Most women either had no prior HPV testing recorded or had consistently HPV-negative results, while HPV positivity was observed in a smaller subgroup.

item.title: Long-Term Outcomes of IDH2-Mutant Sinonasal Carcinomas Compared With IDH2-Wild Type Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Scholfield DW, Axiotakis L, Woods R, Tai K, Eagan A, Boe LA, Finnegan E, Tam K, Cracchiolo J, Dunn L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Scholfield DW, Axiotakis L, Woods R, Tai K, Eagan A, Boe LA, Finnegan E, Tam K, Cracchiolo J, Dunn L, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70495
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42855994



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal carcinomas are aggressive and often locally invasive at presentation, with no universally accepted treatment approach. Histopathologic IDH2-mutant status appears to be associated with improved treatment response and survival. However, the clinical significance of histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas, as well as that of IDH2 mutation status within SNUC, remains unclear and long-term clinical outcome data are limited. METHODS: Records from a prospectively maintained skull-base database at a large, tertiary care hospital system from 1986 to 2024 were reviewed. Patients with a diagnosis of SNUC or sinonasal tumor of any histopathology positive for IDH2 R172 mutation were identified. SMARCB1-deficient, SMARCA4-deficient, NUT sinonasal carcinomas, and other small round cell mimickers were excluded. After histopathologic confirmation, 22 IDH2-mutant SNUC, 14 IDH2-mutant non-SNUC, and 8 IDH2-wildtype SNUC cases were amenable to comprehensive clinicopathologic data review. A presence of IDH2 R172 and pathogenic TP53 mutations was determined by molecular testing and/or by immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 58 years and 61% of patients were male. The majority of patients presented with T4b disease (41% of IDH2-mutant SNUC; 57% of IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.3). There was no significant difference in the proportion of patients presenting with orbital invasion (55% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 64% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7) or intracranial invasion (82% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 79% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7). On histopathology, there was no significant difference in perineural invasion and margin status between the three subgroups (p > 0.6). A greater proportion of IDH2-mutant non-SNUCs had TP53 mutations (67%) than IDH2-mutant SNUC (31%) and IDH2-wildtype SNUC (29%) (p = 0.13). Across the cohort, 41% of patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with a partial response by RECIST criteria in 94% of patients across the subgroups. Median follow-up was 28 months (IQR 11-64 months). 5-year DSS of 73% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 75% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 80% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). 5-year RFS was 53% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 48% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 43% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). CONCLUSION: Upfront assessment of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients may be warranted to select patients for clinical trials with IDH-inhibitors. However, no significant differences in the extent of disease at presentation or response to induction chemotherapy were observed according to histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas or IDH2 mutation status within SNUC. Larger series are required to determine the prognostic significance of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients.

item.title: Mohs vs. Wide Local Excision for Early-Stage (AJCC 0-II) Cutaneous Head and Neck Melanoma: A Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Ardoin A, Vasudevan SS, Rodrigues KC, Vance CJ, Pou JD, Nathan CO
item.description:
Authors: Ardoin A, Vasudevan SS, Rodrigues KC, Vance CJ, Pou JD, Nathan CO
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70511
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42855971



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare oncologic outcomes of Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) versus wide local excision (WLE) in the management of cutaneous head and neck melanoma (CHNM), including melanoma in situ (MIS) and Stage I-II invasive disease. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science were systematically searched for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026 that reported outcomes of MMS versus WLE for CHNM, including MIS and AJCC Stage I-II invasive disease. Outcomes of interest were recurrence, tumor upstaging, and secondary excision rates, which were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis model. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness, and meta-regression was used to explore sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: Of 691 records screened, 23 studies comprising 7090 cases of early-stage (AJCC Stage 0-II) CHNM were included. The median age was 68.8 years, and 68.4% of patients were male. For MIS, the pooled local recurrence rate was lower after MMS (1.7%; 95% CI: 0.7-4.4) than after WLE (6.3%; 95% CI: 3.4-11.4). Upstaging to invasive melanoma was likewise less frequent with MMS (3.3%; 95% CI: 2.1-4.9) than with WLE (8.1%; 95% CI: 4.3-14.8), as was secondary surgical excision (1.2%; 95% CI: 0.1-10.3 vs. 9.7%; 95% CI: 3.0-27.0). Among Stage I-II cases, the pooled recurrence rate was 1.3% (95% CI: 0.3-4.6) after MMS and 8.8% (95% CI: 1.3-41.0) after WLE. CONCLUSION: Although none of the between-group differences reached statistical significance, MMS showed consistently favorable trends in local control and in reducing upstaging and secondary procedures for early-stage CHNM. These findings support consideration of MMS in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Treatment pathways for oral tongue or floor of mouth reconstruction: A comparative analysis of islanded facial artery myomucosal flap and free anterolateral thigh flap.
item.dc:creator: Lin X, Han X, Wang M, Shao X, Du Z, Song B, Liu H
item.description:
Authors: Lin X, Han X, Wang M, Shao X, Du Z, Song B, Liu H
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108173
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42854362



Abstract:
PURPOSE: The free anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap is the mainstay for reconstructing intraoral defects after oral tongue (OT) or floor of mouth (FOM) squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) resection, but the islanded facial artery myomucosal (iFAMM) flap has emerged as an alternative for selected patients. This study compared perioperative outcomes, functional recovery, and hospitalization costs between the two reconstructive pathways in cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing resection of cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC with reconstruction using either the iFAMM or free ALT flap. Baseline characteristics, operative duration, complications, functional outcomes (mouth opening, swallowing, speech), esthetic outcomes, and hospitalization costs were compared, with effect sizes (95% CI) and multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: Among 31 patients, 16 received iFAMM flap-based pathway treatment (iFAMM pathway) and 15 received free ALT flap-based pathway treatment (ALT pathway). While functional outcomes were comparable, the iFAMM pathway showed shorter operative time (514.4 ± 66.2 vs. 602.6 ± 95.2 min, p = 0.005), higher aesthetic VAS score (6.8 ± 1.5 vs. 4.9 ± 1.3, p = 0.001), and lower costs (8,848.7 ± 2,075.1 USD vs. 14,212.5 ± 2,719.9 USD, p < 0.0001). Multivariable regression confirmed flap-based pathway as an independent predictor for all the three primary outcomes. CONCLUSION: The iFAMM pathway appears to be a promising alternative to the ALT pathway for surgical treatment of cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC with comparable function, superior aesthetics, and lower costs. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in prospective trials.

item.title: Phase I/II Study of Bavdegalutamide, a Proteolysis-Targeting Chimera Androgen Receptor Degrader, in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Gao X, Garmezy B, Vuky J, Shen J, Sartor O, Sternberg CN, Dreicer R, Hussain M, Rezazadeh Kalebasty A, Percent IJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Gao X, Garmezy B, Vuky J, Shen J, Sartor O, Sternberg CN, Dreicer R, Hussain M, Rezazadeh Kalebasty A, Percent IJ, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-25-02995
Published: 2026-Oct-09

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This phase I/II study (which, to our knowledge, is the first such study in humans) evaluated the safety and efficacy of bavdegalutamide (ARV-110), a proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) androgen receptor (AR) degrader, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients were adult (18 years and older) males with mCRPC previously treated with an AR pathway inhibitor (ARPI). In phase I, patients received escalating doses of oral bavdegalutamide to determine the recommended phase II dose (RP2D). In phase II, patients received bavdegalutamide at the RP2D in 28-day cycles. Antitumor activity, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response rate (≥50% [PSA50] or ≥30% [PSA30] decline from baseline) and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS), was assessed in three AR molecular profile-defined subgroups and a less-pretreated (one prior ARPI without prior chemotherapy) subgroup. RESULTS: In phase I (N = 95), bavdegalutamide 420 mg once daily was the RP2D. In phase II, PSA50 and PSA30 rates, respectively, were 60.0% and 70.0% among patients with tumors harboring AR T878 and/or H875 mutations (n = 20), 4.3% and 6.5% among those with wild-type AR or other AR alterations (n = 46), and 3.1% and 6.3% among those with AR L702H mutations or AR splice variant 7 expression (n = 32); the median rPFS was 11.1, 4.2, and 5.1 months in the respective subgroups. Among less-pretreated patients (n = 42), the PSA50 rate was 21.4%, the PSA30 rate was 23.8%, and the median rPFS was 11.1 months. Among phase II patients (n = 144), 72.3% experienced grade 1/2 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and 17.4% experienced grade 3 TRAEs; no grade ≥4 TRAEs occurred. TRAEs led to dose reduction and discontinuation in 11.8% and 11.1% of patients, respectively. CONCLUSION: Bavdegalutamide had a manageable safety profile and showed promising clinical activity in patients with mCRPC, particularly those with tumors harboring AR T878/H875 mutations.

item.title: Environmental noise pollution and its association with temporomandibular joint disorders, malocclusion, and bruxism: A Comparative cross-sectional study of adults in high-traffic and low- traffic areas.
item.dc:creator: Hasan A Alshehri A, Ali F Alshadidi A, Aldosari LIN, Kaleem SM, Gurumurthy V, Vyas R, Vaddamanu SK
item.description:
Authors: Hasan A Alshehri A, Ali F Alshadidi A, Aldosari LIN, Kaleem SM, Gurumurthy V, Vyas R, Vaddamanu SK
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360667
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42853839



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic environmental noise exposure is a recognized public health concern linked to stress-mediated physiological responses, yet its specific impact on temporomandibular disorders (TMD), bruxism, and malocclusion remains poorly investigated. OBJECTIVES: To compare the prevalence of TMD, malocclusion, and bruxism between adults residing in high-traffic versus Low- traffic areas in New Delhi, India, and to identify independent predictors of TMD risk. METHODS: This comparative cross-sectional study enrolled 300 adults (150 per group) from high traffic and low traffic residential areas of New Delhi, India. Individual-level noise exposure (LAeq,24h) was objectively measured. TMD was diagnosed using Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD Axis I criteria). Bruxism, malocclusion, perceived stress scale -1= (PSS-10), and Pittsburgh sleep quality (PSQI) were assessed using validated instruments. Multivariable logistic regression and mediation analysis were performed. RESULTS: High-traffic residents had significantly higher TMD prevalence (61.3% vs. 25.3%), bruxism (42.7% vs. 14.0%), and malocclusion (52.0% vs. 26.0%; all p < 0.001). A significant dose-response relationship was confirmed (χ² for trend p < 0.001). High noise exposure was the strongest independent predictor of TMD (aOR = 3.10; 95% CI: 2.00-4.80). Bruxism and perceived stress accounted for 41.4% of this association in exploratory mediation analysis, a pattern compatible with mediation, though the cross sectional design precludes establishing temporal precedence. CONCLUSIONS: Environmental noise exposure was independently and dose-dependently associated with TMD andbruxism. malocclusion was also prevalent in high traffic areas; however, this cross sectional association more likely reflects pre-existing skeletal or occlusal characteristics than a causal effect of noise, and should be interpreted with caution. These findings support noise abatement policies and targeted oral health screening in high traffic urban environments.

item.title: Facial and oral factors affecting smiles in young people.
item.dc:creator: Pham TAV, Le PP, Nguyen VPP
item.description:
Authors: Pham TAV, Le PP, Nguyen VPP
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360529
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42853835



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize smile morphology and examine its associations with facial and oral parameters, with emphasis on factors associated with smile attractiveness in Vietnamese young adults. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Dynamic smiles of 490 Vietnamese individuals (mean age 21.04 ± 1.79 years) were recorded and analyzed. Categorical smile characteristics including anterior smile line, smile arc, upper lip curvature, most posterior tooth displayed, and upper teeth-lower lip relationship were assessed. Quantitative parameters comprised buccal corridor space, smile index, and dynamic smile symmetry. Multiple facial and dentofacial measurements were also obtained, including upper lip length, lip mobility, philtrum height, proportional indices, lip-line and occlusal plane cant, dental midline deviation, mouth size ratio, and incisal edge visibility. Participants were further classified according to smile attractiveness to identify associated determinants. RESULTS: The anterior smile line, smile arc, and upper lip curvature demonstrated broad associations with several dentofacial parameters. The most posterior tooth displayed was significantly related to the philtrum height-upper lip length ratio and incisal edge visibility. Buccal corridor space and smile index showed comparatively limited correlations. Dynamic smile symmetry was significantly associated with upper lip length during smiling and mouth size ratio at rest. Several soft tissue and dentofacial variables were identified as contributing factors to smile attractiveness. CONCLUSION: Smile morphology in Vietnamese young adults is influenced by coordinated interactions between soft tissue dynamics and dentofacial proportions. These findings highlight population-specific characteristics and provide clinically relevant guidance for aesthetic evaluation and treatment planning in orthodontic and restorative practice.

item.title: An urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Y, Wu H, Yang T, Sun J, Li H, Zhu W
item.description:
Authors: Jiang Y, Wu H, Yang T, Sun J, Li H, Zhu W
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360432
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42853817



Abstract:
Accurate assessment of urban patrol cases plays an important role in maintaining urban safety and improving the efficiency of urban governance. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.

item.title: A dual-functional antiviral and anticancer peptide to target intricate host-pathogen interacting proteins of human papillomavirus associated with head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Ashok G, Ghosh S, Sengupta S, Bhattacharya B, Jana P, Livingstone P, Ramaiah S, Anbarasu A
item.description:
Authors: Ashok G, Ghosh S, Sengupta S, Bhattacharya B, Jana P, Livingstone P, Ramaiah S, Anbarasu A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359513
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42853814



Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is increasingly being reported worldwide, and a major contributing factor is the incidence of human papillomavirus infections. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. An efficient way to block the virus-induced carcinogenesis is to identify a common medicament that can effectively inhibit the viral and host proteins. In the present study, HNSCC transcriptomic profiles and HPV genes involved in host-pathogen interactions were retrieved. The overexpressed HNSCC genes were further considered for host-pathogen and protein-protein interaction network analyses. Validated viral and host hub-genes were then docked with antiviral peptides with anticancer activities and subjected to simulation studies. Interactome analyses identified CDK1, CCNA2, CAV1, BRCA1, TERT and EGFR as host hub-genes, while E5_HPV16, E6_HPV33, E7_HPV16, 18 and 33 were screened as viral hub-genes. Functional, clinical, mutational and survival analyses filtered CDK1, CCNA2 and CAV1 as potential host therapeutic targets. Four antiviral-anticancer peptides were filtered after physico-chemical screening, which were docked with the host and viral proteins. Among them, peptide 4 (AP02569) was identified to have a high average binding affinity with an average binding energy of -1048.01 kcal/mol across all targets. The molecular dynamics simulations of peptide 4 demonstrated the overall stability among the docked complexes of all targets. It further indicated that peptide 4 had minimal fluctuation across all the docked complexes, and MM-GBSA analysis showed that peptide 4 was able to form energetically stable complexes with all target proteins. Our findings suggest that dual-functional antiviral and anticancer compounds can be potent therapeutic interventions for viral-led carcinogenesis in head and neck cancer.

item.title: Cell Line Authentication Reveals HeLa-Derived Contamination of SACC-83 and SACC-LM in Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Research.
item.dc:creator: Chen C, Zhao X, Chen X, Gao Y
item.description:
Authors: Chen C, Zhao X, Chen X, Gao Y
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70771
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42853703



Abstract:
SACC-83 was established in 1990 from a patient with adenoid cystic carcinoma, with SACC-LM as its lung-metastatic subline derived through in vivo selection in nude mice. Although several other purported ACC cell lines have already been reported as cross-contaminated, the true origin of SACC-83 and SACC-LM has remained unclear despite their wide use in the field. To address this, we carried out short tandem repeat (STR) profiling on 10 SACC-83 and SACC-LM samples submitted from six independent laboratories across China during our routine authentication work. Statistical analysis using the classic Tanabe comparison algorithm on the CLASTR website returned matches to multiple common cell line contaminants. Among these, comparison with HeLa yielded a random match probability (RMP) of 1.29 × 10-19 and a likelihood ratio (LR) of 7.75 × 1018. These findings provide direct evidence that both SACC-83 and SACC-LM are HeLa-derived contaminants rather than authentic SACC models. We therefore recommend that researchers suspend further use of these two lines and highlight the broader role that independent authentication platforms, by virtue of their direct access to cell line data, can play as an effective early-warning system against misidentification in the scientific community.

item.title: Radiofrequency Ablation of Calcified Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma: Long-Term Imaging Evolution and Clinical Outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Jeong SY, Baek SM, Shin S, Kim H, Suh YH, Baek JH
item.description:
Authors: Jeong SY, Baek SM, Shin S, Kim H, Suh YH, Baek JH
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261494905
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42853595



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a minimally invasive treatment for low-risk papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC). Although intratumoral calcification is a common feature of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), its impact on RFA efficacy remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility, clinical outcomes, and pattern-specific course of calcification resolution with RFA for PTMC. METHODS: This retrospective study included 258 consecutive patients with low-risk, unifocal PTMC who underwent RFA between November 2017 and August 2022. Intratumoral calcification was classified on ultrasonography as microcalcification, macrocalcification, rim calcification, or mixed calcification. The primary outcomes were technical success and calcification disappearance rates by calcification pattern. Secondary outcomes included serial volume reduction ratio (VRR), cumulative disease progression, local tumor recurrence, and complications. RESULTS: Among 258 PTMCs, 94 had calcifications (68 microcalcifications, 12 macrocalcifications, 14 rim calcifications) and 164 had none. Mean follow-up was 53.5 ± 16.7 months. Technical success was achieved in all patients in both groups. By 18 months, mean VRR exceeded 90% in both groups, and all tumors achieved 100% VRR at the final follow-up (≥36 months). Cumulative disease progression occurred in one patient (0.4%, lymph node metastases at ipsilateral neck level IV and VI), and 15 patients (5.8%) developed new PTC in the remaining thyroid; the rates did not differ between groups. Among PTMCs with calcifications, complete disappearance of calcification occurred in 90 cases (90/94, 95.7%) after 14.2 ± 12.3 months. Disappearance rates were highest for microcalcifications (100%), followed by rim calcifications (92.9%) and macrocalcifications (75.0%). Microcalcifications were resolved significantly faster (mean, 12.0 months), whereas rim calcifications were resolved the slowest (mean, 24.8 months; p < 0.001). The solid component and calcification resolved concurrently in 75.5% of tumors. One minor complication (transient hoarseness, 0.4%) occurred, and no major or delayed complications were observed. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, RFA achieved complete resolution of the viable soft-tissue component with a low complication rate in low-risk PTMC, both with and without intratumoral calcification. Technical success was achieved in 100% of tumors regardless of calcification status, and no significant difference in outcomes was observed between the calcified and noncalcified groups. These findings suggest that intratumoral calcification does not preclude effective ablation.

item.title: Voice Outcomes Following Thermal Ablation for Thyroid Nodules: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Mouratidou S, Dabab N, Habib A, Seif-Elnasr M, Rovira A, Simo R
item.description:
Authors: Mouratidou S, Dabab N, Habib A, Seif-Elnasr M, Rovira A, Simo R
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70502

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate voice outcomes following thermal ablation techniques for the management of benign and malignant thyroid nodules. DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature review of PubMed and Embase databases was performed up to March 2025. REVIEW METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Inclusion criteria were studies with adult patients undergoing thermal ablation for thyroid nodules with reported objective voice outcomes. Data extracted included study characteristics, patient demographics, ablation modality, and objective and subjective voice outcomes. RESULTS: Eighteen studies comprising 5168 patients were included. Ablation modalities were radiofrequency ablation, microwave ablation, laser ablation, and high-intensity focused ultrasound. Objective pre-procedural assessment of vocal cord function using fibreoptic nasoendoscopy or sonographic evaluation was reported in 2054 patients (39.7%). Post-procedural objective vocal cord assessment was most commonly performed in symptomatic cases, while assessment was routinely performed irrespective of symptoms in 2110 patients (40.8%). The pooled post-procedural vocal cord palsy rate was 1.4%, with most cases being transient. Permanent vocal cord palsy was rare (n = 2, 0.05%). Subjective voice symptoms without objective vocal cord dysfunction were generally mild and self-limiting. CONCLUSION: Thermal ablation of thyroid nodules is associated with a low risk of clinically significant voice complications. Most voice changes are transient, although the lack of standardized voice assessment likely underestimates true complication rates. Routine objective laryngeal evaluation and standardized reporting are essential to ensure accurate detection of voice complications, optimize patient counseling, and enhance the safety of thyroid ablation practice.

Abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to examine the factors associated with psychological resilience in Sjögren's disease. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 83 patients (F/M: 79/4). Hyposalivation was observed in 41%, while Schirmer's test positivity was observed in 84.3% of patients. Scores of the Brief Resilience Scale, self-reported general health, self-reported oral health, EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI), and physician global assessment for disease activity were noted. A mediation analysis was performed to examine the relationships among these variables. RESULTS: Lower BRS scores were associated with Schirmer's test positivity and reduced salivary flow rate, higher scores of ESSPRI, physician and patient global assessments of disease activity (p < 0.05). In the simple mediation analysis, a lower BRS score as the dependent variable was directly associated with a higher physician-assessed global disease activity as the independent variable and indirectly associated with the higher ESSPRI score as a mediator variable (p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Since ocular dryness, lower salivary flow rates, physician global assessment of disease activity, and ESSPRI reflecting patient-reported symptom severity were identified as key contributors to lower levels of psychological resilience in Sjögren's disease, these measures may offer clinicians valuable guidance for tailoring more effective, patient-centered integrated multidisciplinary care strategies for patients with SjD.

Published: 2026-Oct-09

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Conventional topical therapies for oral ulcers remain limited due to poor mucosal adhesion and rapid clearance by saliva. To overcome these challenges, we aimed to develop a microneedle patch with α-boswellic acid for targeted anti-inflammatory treatment of oral ulcers. METHODS: The microneedle patch was fabricated and evaluated for mechanical strength and drug release profile. Biocompatibility was assessed. In vitro anti-inflammatory activity was examined in macrophages. In vivo efficacy was tested using a rat oral ulcer model. RESULTS: The α-boswellic acid-loaded hyaluronic acid methacryloyl microneedle patch displayed adequate mechanical properties and sustained drug release. It exhibited favorable biocompatibility with low cytotoxicity and no apparent adverse effects on fibroblast migration. In vitro, the patch significantly inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokine and promoted M2 polarization. The patch accelerated ulcer healing, reducing the unhealed wound area in vivo. Enhanced collagen deposition and stimulated neovascularization were observed. Histological results demonstrated organized tissue regeneration, decreased neutrophil infiltration, and shifted macrophage phenotype. This approach addresses key limitations of current topical treatments, demonstrating a promising therapeutic strategy for clinical translation.

item.title: Confocal Ex Vivo Margin Assessment in Transoral Laser Cordectomy: A Pilot Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
item.dc:creator: Alberti C, Fabbri VP, Eccher A, Marchioni D, Liberale C, Baldelli S, Morselli G, Ciuffreda R, Delvecchio F, Mattioli F
item.description:
Authors: Alberti C, Fabbri VP, Eccher A, Marchioni D, Liberale C, Baldelli S, Morselli G, Ciuffreda R, Delvecchio F, Mattioli F
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70972

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Margin assessment in transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) for glottic squamous cell carcinoma is challenging due to specimen size, fragmentation, and artifacts. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary diagnostic performance of the Histolog Scanner, an ultra-fast ex vivo confocal microscopy system, for intraoperative margin assessment in TLM cordectomy. METHODS: This prospective pilot study evaluated adult patients undergoing TLM cordectomy for glottic squamous cell carcinoma. Five predefined margins per specimen (anterior, posterior, superior, inferior, deep) were evaluated using Histolog Scanner and compared with conventional hematoxylin and eosin histopathology, used as the reference standard. Concordance, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and diagnostic accuracy were assessed. RESULTS: Nineteen patients were included, yielding to 95 evaluable margins. Overall concordance between Histolog Scanner and histopathology was 92.6% (88/95 margins). The scanner identified 12 true-positive, 76 true-negative, five false-positive, and two false-negative margins. Sensitivity was 85.7% (95% CI: 57.2-98.2), specificity 93.8% (95% CI: 86.2-98.0), positive predictive value 70.6% (95% CI: 44.0-89.7), negative predictive value 97.4% (95% CI: 91.0-99.7), and accuracy 92.6% (95% CI: 85.4-97.0). Agreement was substantial (Cohen's kappa = 0.73). Mean acquisition time was 13 min per specimen. CONCLUSION: The Histolog Scanner is a feasible, rapid intraoperative screening tool with high specificity and excellent negative predictive value for ruling out involved margins in TLM cordectomy. It serves as an intraoperative adjunct rather than a replacement for definitive histopathology, which remains essential. Larger multicenter studies are required before widespread clinical setting implementation.

item.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-08
PMID: 42849489



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks. METHODS: RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation. INTERPRETATION: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.
