Abstract:
Oral contraceptives (OCs) are composed of artificial estrogen (ethinyl-estradiol) and/or progesterone (progestin), which can attach to receptors in the brain and potentially influence cognition. One prior study suggested that OC use was associated with increased mind-wandering - implying that OC use was associated with detriments to attention. In contrast, two subsequent well-powered conceptual replications of this initial finding revealed little evidence that OC use was related to increases in inattentiveness (including mind-wandering). However, these later studies collapsed across different OC formulations, which may obscure effects specific to particular formulations. In the present study, we investigated the possibility that OC formulation might differentially relate to attention-related traits. To do this, we collected trait-level reports of the tendency to experience attention related errors, attention lapses, spontaneous and deliberate mind-wandering, boredom, and flow in undergraduate females using OCs, and we collected the brand of OC used from which it was possible to derive the formulation. OC formulations differed in ethinyl-estradiol dose, progestin dose, dosing schedule, hormonal activity (or potency), and the type (or 'generation') of progestin used. We found no evidence that different OC formulations were related to differences in attention-related traits, which suggests that OC users can be treated as a homogenous group when examining trait-level attention. Comparisons of OC users (collapsing across formulation) to non-users again revealed no significant differences in trait-level attention.

item.title: Spatial organization of HPV-associated immune programs across tissue compartments in oropharyngeal cancer.
item.dc:creator: Wakisaka N, Moriyama-Kita M, Kondo S, Nakanishi Y, Endo K, Sugimoto H, Yoshizaki T
item.description:
Authors: Wakisaka N, Moriyama-Kita M, Kondo S, Nakanishi Y, Endo K, Sugimoto H, Yoshizaki T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0356717
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42837361



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is characterized by a distinct immune microenvironment; however, the biological significance of immune-related transcriptional programs may vary according to their spatial localization. We investigated the spatial organization of HPV-associated transcriptional programs across anatomically distinct tissue compartments in OPC. METHODS: An oropharynx-restricted The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) cohort comprising 77 tumors (51 HPV-positive and 26 HPV-negative) was analyzed using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Spatial transcriptomic profiling using GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiling was evaluated in lymphoid follicular regions (LFRs) and tumor tissue regions (TTRs) from six OPC patients (four HPV-positive and two HPV-negative), with the patient treated as the primary experimental unit. Tumor-free surrounding palatine tonsillar tissue (PTT) was analyzed in an independent microarray cohort comprising 23 HPV-positive and four HPV-negative cases. Eight prespecified immune- and metabolism-related transcriptional programs were evaluated, with additional exploratory cell-type deconvolution and overall survival analyses. RESULTS: In TCGA-OPSCC, all five immune-related programs were higher in HPV-positive tumors, and Stem-like, Tpex, B-cell activity, and T-cell activity remained significantly associated with HPV-positive status after adjustment for clinicopathological covariates and FDR correction. In paired GeoMx analyses, all five immune-related programs were higher in LFRs than in TTRs in all six patients, whereas Estrogen Response Early and Estrogen Response Late were higher in TTRs in all six patients (BH-FDR = 0.0357 for each program). Bile Acid Metabolism showed no consistent compartment-specific difference. HPV-associated differences within individual GeoMx compartments and HPV-by-compartment interactions were not statistically significant after FDR correction. In PTT, immune-related and metabolic programs showed directional HPV-associated differences, but none remained significant after FDR correction. Higher scores for several immune-related programs were associated with improved overall survival in univariable TCGA-OPSCC analyses, but these associations were attenuated after accounting for HPV status. CONCLUSIONS: HPV-associated immune transcriptional programs identified in bulk OPC show consistent spatial organization across lymphoid follicular and tumor tissue compartments. The most robust spatial feature was within-patient compartmentalization between LFRs and TTRs, whereas evidence for HPV-associated differences within individual spatial compartments was limited. These findings emphasize the importance of anatomical context when interpreting transcriptional programs in OPC.

item.title: A genetic algorithm-optimized EWMA control chart integrating machine learning-based risk prediction for multistage thyroid cancer treatment monitoring.
item.dc:creator: Rasouli M, Rahimi E, Ilaty A
item.description:
Authors: Rasouli M, Rahimi E, Ilaty A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0347876
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42837336



Abstract:
Effective monitoring of thyroid cancer treatment requires timely detection of clinically meaningful changes across complex, multistage care pathways. Traditional monitoring approaches often rely on static thresholds and periodic assessments, limiting their sensitivity to subtle yet important process deviations and potentially delaying clinical intervention. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated, data-driven framework that combines deep learning-based risk prediction with genetic algorithm-optimized statistical process monitoring to enhance thyroid cancer treatment surveillance. Informative clinical variables were first identified using the Information Functions algorithm, and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network was then employed to predict patient-specific treatment risk, capturing nonlinear relationships within longitudinal electronic medical record data. The resulting risk estimates were sequentially incorporated into Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) control charts to enable continuous process monitoring. To further improve chart performance, a genetic algorithm was used to optimize EWMA parameters, enhancing accuracy and sensitivity while maintaining chart stability. The results demonstrate that the MLP model outperforms conventional machine learning approaches in risk prediction across multiple evaluation metrics. Genetic algorithm-optimized EWMA charts exhibit smoother trajectories, improved stability, and more reliable detection of clinically meaningful deviations compared with non-optimized charts. The consistency of these improvements across multiple features suggests that GA-based optimization enhances overall control chart performance rather than feature-specific behavior. This hybrid framework demonstrates the feasibility of integrating machine learning-derived risk prediction with optimized statistical process control for longitudinal treatment monitoring. The proposed approach supports proactive treatment surveillance, risk-stratified follow-up, timely clinical intervention, and data-driven decision-making in thyroid cancer care. Furthermore, the framework has the potential to enable continuous and adaptive monitoring across complex multi-stage treatment pathways if integrated with electronic medical record (EMR) systems in future implementations.

item.title: Primary Tumor Location and Lymphatic Spread in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Fournier I, Zafereo ME, Hamidi S, Sturgis EM, Waguespack SG, Williams MD, Hosseini SM, Hu MI, Graham PH, Banuchi V, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Fournier I, Zafereo ME, Hamidi S, Sturgis EM, Waguespack SG, Williams MD, Hosseini SM, Hu MI, Graham PH, Banuchi V, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70474
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42836563



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) frequently metastasizes to cervical lymph nodes. Surgical planning is often based on the presumed central-to-lateral pattern of spread. The extent of central and lateral neck dissection remains controversial, with recommendations largely derived from small series. The study aimed to determine whether primary tumor location can guide the extent of neck dissection. STUDY DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Quaternary care center. METHODS: Patients with PTC undergoing primary thyroid surgery with a central and/or lateral neck dissection (CND and/or LND) between 1999 and 2023 were evaluated. Tumor location (superior, mid, inferior pole, or isthmus) was determined by ultrasound and confirmed on pathology. The primary outcome was pattern of nodal metastases by tumor location. RESULTS: Among 1688 patients (median age 45 years; 67% female), 99% underwent CND and 45% LND. Central neck positivity was similar across superior (79%; 262/333), inferior (73%; 286/393), mid (74%; 626/849), and isthmic (76%; 71/94) tumors (P = .22). On multivariable logistic regression, central neck positivity did not differ significantly (superior OR: 1.28 [95% CI, 0.74-2.23]; lower OR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.52-1.50]; mid OR, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.48-1.32]; compared with isthmic. LND unadjusted and adjusted positivity rates were also comparable across primary tumor location. In patients undergoing LND, level III was most frequently involved (81%), followed by levels IV (75%), IIa (60%), Vb (36%), and IIb (9%) (P < .01). Lastly, superior pole tumors were significantly associated with ipsilateral level III involvement, compared with inferior and mid pole tumors (P < .01). CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing therapeutic neck dissection for PTC, primary tumor location did not predict nodal distribution and should not determine the extent of neck dissection.

item.title: Optimal Sequencing of First-Line Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors With Definitive Chemoradiotherapy: A Multicenter Real-World Cohort Study Comparing Induction, Concurrent, and Consolidation Strategies for Unresectable Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Zhao X, Wen S, Song C, Wang J, Zhang Y, Wang C, Liu Y, Qian P, Cao J, Hou Q, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70740
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42836385



Abstract:
While first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) combined with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) represent a crucial advancement for unresectable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), the optimal sequencing of these modalities remains unresolved. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of induction, concurrent, and consolidation ICI strategies, this multicenter real-world cohort study enrolled 662 patients with Stage II-IVA unresectable ESCC across 12 cancer centers. Patients were categorized into induction (IC-CRT), concurrent (ICRT), and consolidation (CRT-IC) groups, with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) applied to balance baseline characteristics. Following IPTW adjustment, the median overall survival (OS) in the IC-CRT, ICRT, and CRT-IC groups was 34.7 months, not reached, and 23.1 months, respectively (p = 0.016), while the corresponding median progression-free survival (PFS) times were 20.1, 25.3, and 12.9 months, respectively (p = 0.014). Among the three sequencing strategies, ICRT achieved the most favorable survival outcomes, followed by IC-CRT and CRT-IC. Multivariable Cox regression confirmed that ICRT was associated with a significantly reduced risk of mortality compared with IC-CRT (HR = 0.71, p = 0.046) and CRT-IC (HR = 0.53, adjusted p < 0.001). Safety profiles indicated that ICRT carried the highest burden of Grade 3-4 treatment-related pneumonitis (7.7%). In conclusion, ICRT as a first-line treatment for locally advanced ESCC showed the most favorable survival profile compared with induction or consolidation sequencing, although its higher toxicity profile necessitates careful patient selection and proactive clinical management. In contrast, the CRT-IC strategy exhibited the best tolerability but the least favorable survival outcome.

item.title: Systemic Inflammatory Ratios Predict Survival in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Gavrielov I, Dobriyan A, Shavit I, Vered M
item.description:
Authors: Gavrielov I, Dobriyan A, Shavit I, Vered M
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70515
Published: 2026-Oct-05
PMID: 42834691



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of the systemic inflammation-related biomarkers of neutrophil-lymphocyte, albumin-globulin, lymphocyte-monocyte, and platelet-lymphocyte ratios at three perioperative time points, and to explore their association with clinicopathologic features and disease-specific survival. METHODS: In 220 oral squamous cell carcinoma patients undergoing surgery (2012-2023), we assessed risk factors, such as extranodal extension, TNM stage, and biomarker cutoffs (neutrophil-lymphocyte 5.0; albumin-globulin 1.21; lymphocyte-monocyte 3.14; platelet-lymphocyte 218.9). Disease-specific survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox multivariate models. Significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Biomarkers measured 3 months postoperatively were the strongest predictors. Multivariate analysis identified high neutrophil-lymphocyte (HR = 2.99, 95% CI 1.44-6.21; p = 0.003), low albumin-globulin (HR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.89; p = 0.023) ratios, and extranodal extension (HR = 3.17, 95% CI 1.54-6.52; p = 0.002) as independent predictors of poorer disease-specific survival. Importantly, neutrophil-lymphocyte prognostic impact was comparable to that of extranodal extension, a well-established pathological risk factor. CONCLUSIONS: Three months post-surgery, high neutrophil-lymphocyte and low albumin-globulin ratios independently predict worse disease-specific survival in oral cancer. Neutrophil-lymphocyte, a simple and widely available biomarker, offers prognostic insight comparable to extranodal extension, supporting its integration into postoperative risk stratification and potentially guiding adjuvant therapy decisions.

item.title: Oral Ulcerations and Phytotherapy: Potential Role of Helichrysum Essential Oil-A Literature Review.
item.dc:creator: Ivkovic R, Antic R, Majumder A, Majumder S, Stanisic D
item.description:
Authors: Ivkovic R, Antic R, Majumder A, Majumder S, Stanisic D
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70531
Published: 2026-Oct-05
PMID: 42834680



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) is a common yet therapeutically challenging chronic inflammatory disease of the oral mucosa, characterized by recurrent, painful ulcerations that substantially affect patients' quality of life. OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes current evidence on phytotherapy in RAS, with particular focus on the potential therapeutic relevance of Helichrysum italicum essential oil (HI EO). FINDINGS AND DISCUSSION: Phytotherapy has been investigated as a therapeutic option for RAS, primarily due to its reported ability to reduce pain, shorten healing time, and promote ulcer resolution. Additionally, some phytotherapeutic preparations may offer a favorable tolerability profile, although their safety and comparative efficacy require further evaluation. Phytotherapy may therefore be considered as an adjunctive or complementary approach in the management of RAS. Previous research on HI EO provides a biological rationale for investigating its potential relevance to oral mucosal healing. However, its potential role in RAS remains hypothetical because direct clinical evidence regarding its efficacy and safety is currently lacking. This hypothesis therefore requires further investigation in clinical studies. CONCLUSION: Phytotherapy represents a potential supplementary approach to RAS management. The therapeutic potential of HI EO requires validation through rigorously designed preclinical and clinical studies evaluating its efficacy, safety, and clinical relevance.

item.title: Osteosarcoma of the Jaws in Latin America: A Retrospective Multicenter Series of 119 Cases.
item.dc:creator: Drumond VZ, de Arruda JAA, Villaroel-Dorrego M, Dos Reis LA, Sampaio GC, Schuch LF, Menna-Barreto CL, Martins MD, Goulart PC, Souza GG, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-05

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Epidemiological and survival data on osteosarcoma of the jaws (OSJ) in Latin America remain scarce. We characterized the clinicopathological, radiographic, treatment-related, and survival features of OSJ in Latin America. METHODS: This multicenter case series involved 22 institutions from Brazil, Chile, Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela, Uruguay, and Mexico. Demographic, clinical, radiographic, histopathological, treatment, and survival data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression models. RESULTS: A total of 119 OSJ cases were included. The median age was 33 years, with a female predominance (58%), and the mandible was the most commonly affected site (68.9%). A mixed radiographic appearance predominated and was frequently accompanied by cortical perforation and a sunburst periosteal reaction. Histologically, the osteoblastic subtype accounted for 63.5% of cases. Surgical resection was the main treatment modality (71.2%). Increasing age (p = 0.034) and multimodal or nonsurgical management (p = 0.023) were independently associated with poorer survival. The estimated overall survival rates were 67.5% at 12 months and 37.5% at 60 months. CONCLUSION: Data corroborate previous literature and demonstrate that OSJ in Latin America predominantly affects adults and exhibits aggressive patterns. Surgical management remains central to improving survival whenever it is technically feasible.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To propose a clinical classification system for oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) based on lesion characteristics, aiming to enhance early recognition and initial clinical diagnostic hypothesis rate in clinical practice. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 422 OSCC cases was conducted from 2005 to 2023. Lesions were clinically categorized through clinical photographs as either "conventional" (including non-ulcerated plaques; red, white, or mixed and ulcerated infiltrative lesions with raised indurated margins) or "atypical" (different from the one described above) based on their presentation. Atypical cases were further subclassified into morphological types. RESULTS: Of the 422 OSCC cases, 316 (74.9%) were classified as conventional and 106 (25.1%) as atypical. Conventional cases were predominantly ulcerative or leukoplakic, while atypical cases exhibited fissure-like and exophytic patterns. Tongue border was most commonly affected in conventional OSCC, while floor of the mouth and buccal mucosa predominated in atypical forms. CONCLUSION: Approximately one-quarter of OSCC cases present with atypical clinical features. The proposed classification provides a practical tool for clinicians to recognize these variants. However, further prospective validation is warranted to determine whether its application improves clinical recognition and diagnostic accuracy.

Abstract:
We aimed to comprehensively evaluate the associations of a broad panel of systemic inflammation-related biomarkers with overall survival (OS) in metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (mNPC) and to assess whether these signatures mediate the adverse impact of high EBV DNA burden on long-term outcomes. This study included 1847 patients with mNPC treated at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center between 2016 and 2022. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to evaluate associations of inflammation-related indices with OS. Exploratory mediation analyses quantified the extent to which biomarkers partially mediated the association between plasma EBV DNA burden and mortality risk. Mean follow-up was 45.4 months; 713 (38.6%) deaths occurred. Plasma EBV DNA showed stable discrimination (AUCs of 0.63, 0.62, and 0.61 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS). After full adjustment, CALLY and LCR were protective, whereas CAR, NAR, SIRI, IBI, MLR, NC, PC, GPS, mGPS, and LCS were adverse. CAR, CALLY, LCR, IBI, and NC showed the highest discrimination (1-year AUCs, 0.65-0.66). Mediation analyses indicated that MLR, SIRI, CALLY, and NC accounted for 7.6%-9.6% of the EBV DNA load-mortality association. Elevated pretreatment EBV DNA was associated with a coordinated systemic inflammatory profile and worse OS in mNPC. Selected inflammatory markers statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the observed association between EBV DNA burden and mortality. Integrating EBV DNA with inflammatory profiles may improve risk stratification and guide intensified surveillance, earlier assessment, and risk-adapted therapy.

item.title: Outcomes and complications of parathyroidectomy in otorhinolaryngology practice: A single-institution, 10-year retrospective observational study.

Authors: Astl J, Rotnágl J, Holý R, Percik Y, Hložek J

Published: 2026-Oct-03

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parathyroidectomy is associated with a spectrum of potential complications, including recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury, permanent hypocalcemia, postoperative hemorrhage, wound infection, and recurrence of hyperparathyroidism (HPT). The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of 223 parathyroid procedures and to determine the incidence of procedure-related complications. METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed parathyroidectomy cases performed between 2013 and 2022. Demographic data and postoperative complications were collected and assessed. The success rates of surgical removal of parathyroid adenomas, hyperplasia, carcinomas, and cysts were evaluated in relation to preoperative and perioperative diagnostic methods. RESULTS: A total of 223 parathyroidectomy procedures were performed. Unilateral permanent RLN palsy was observed in 0.91% of cases (95% CI, 0.11-3.21%). Bilateral permanent vocal cord palsy was not observed. A positive response to the parathyroidectomy was observed in 98.43% (95% CI, 96.1-99.72%). Temporary hypercalcemia developed in 13.26% (95% CI, 9.41-18.35%). Revision surgery for persistent HPT or recurrence of HPT was necessary in 16 cases. CONCLUSION: The combination of preoperative multimodal imaging and precise hyperparathyroidism diagnosis is essential for reducing the risk of unsuccessful localization in parathyroid surgery. Ultrasound and scintigraphy offers the most effective diagnostic method. Intraoperative neuromonitoring is recommended for revision surgeries.

item.title: YRNA1 expression as a candidate prognostic biomarker in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Fazel F, Koopaie M, Manifar S, Razavi AE, Karamad N
item.description:
Authors: Fazel F, Koopaie M, Manifar S, Razavi AE, Karamad N
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104961
Published: 2026-Oct-03
PMID: 42837795



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (OTSCC) is an aggressive cancer with a 5-year survival of about 60%, highlighting the need for improved molecular risk stratification. Y RNAs (YRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs implicated in tumor progression, but their prognostic role in OTSCC is unclear. This exploratory retrospective cohort study assessed the prognostic value of YRNA1 expression in 26 patients with primary OTSCC who underwent surgical treatment between 2021 and 2022. DESIGN: YRNA1 expression in tumor tissue was quantified using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and associations with clinicopathological features and 3-year disease-specific survival were analyzed using nonparametric tests, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox regression. RESULTS: YRNA1 expression was significantly higher in patients who died within 3 years of surgery than in those surviving beyond 3 years (p = 0.020) and showed a moderate positive correlation with T stage and death during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly poorer survival in patients with high YRNA1 expression compared with those with low expression (log-rank p = 0.020). In an exploratory multivariable Cox model, restricted to T stage and YRNA1 expression to avoid overfitting given the limited number of events (11 deaths), YRNA1 expression showed prognostic potential. Each one-unit increase in log₂-transformed YRNA1 expression was associated with a 43% increase in the hazard of OTSCC-related death (HR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.12-2.03; p = 0.049). However, these findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated YRNA1 expression is associated with poorer disease-specific survival in this cohort of patients with OTSCC, suggesting potential prognostic relevance that requires validation in larger, independent cohorts.

item.title: Development of an MRI-based surgical difficulty scoring system for anterior and deep lobe parotid tumors.
item.dc:creator: Kim JH
item.description:
Authors: Kim JH
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104947
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42863276



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Anterior and deep lobe parotid tumors present substantial technical challenges because of their close relationship to the facial nerve and deep parotid anatomy. We aimed to develop and internally validate a practical MRI-based scoring system to preoperatively predict surgical difficulty in these tumors. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent parotidectomy for anterior or deep lobe tumors between March 2020 and December 2024. A five-domain MRI-based difficulty score (range, 3-15) was constructed based on tumor location, size, relationship to the facial nerve, fat-plane integrity, and multifocality. Surgical difficulty was defined as prolonged operative time exceeding the 75th percentile. Predictive validity was assessed using operative time, estimated blood loss, and postoperative facial nerve outcomes. Interobserver reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Internal validation was performed in a standardized single-surgeon cohort. RESULTS: A total of 149 patients were included. Higher MRI-based difficulty scores were significantly associated with longer operative time and increased estimated blood loss (both p < 0.001). Postoperative facial nerve weakness occurred more frequently with increasing difficulty tiers (p = 0.01). These findings remained consistent in the standardized validation cohort (n = 36). Interobserver reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.87; 95% CI, 0.82-0.91), with minimal mean bias and narrow limits of agreement. CONCLUSIONS: This MRI-based difficulty score reliably predicts surgical complexity in anterior and deep lobe parotid tumors and demonstrates excellent interobserver reproducibility. It may serve as a useful preoperative tool for operative planning and risk stratification. External validation is warranted.

item.title: Executive Summary of the Clinical Practice Guideline on Tinnitus Update.
item.dc:creator: Adams ME, Cramer JD, Tunkel DE, Lee VS, Bourgeois JA, Eshraghi AA, Fagelson MA, White KB, Juliano AF, Kim H, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Adams ME, Cramer JD, Tunkel DE, Lee VS, Bourgeois JA, Eshraghi AA, Fagelson MA, White KB, Juliano AF, Kim H, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70418
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42861486



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tinnitus is the perception of sound without an external source. More than 50 million people in the United States have reported experiencing tinnitus, resulting in an estimated prevalence of 10% to 15% in adults. The focus of this guideline is on tinnitus that is both bothersome and persistent (lasting 6 months or longer), which often negatively affects the patient's quality of life. The target audience for the guideline is any clinician, including allied health professionals, involved in managing patients with tinnitus. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome. PURPOSE: The purpose of this guideline is to provide and update evidence-based recommendations for clinicians managing patients with tinnitus. The target audience for this guideline is any clinician involved in managing patients with tinnitus. People with tinnitus may be evaluated by a variety of health care providers, including primary care clinicians, specialty clinicians, and allied health professionals including audiologists and clinical psychologists. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome. Most people with tinnitus have associated hearing loss, such as sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) secondary to aging (presbycusis), noise exposure (noise-induced hearing loss), or acoustic trauma. Tinnitus can also be a symptom of numerous auditory and non-auditory system disorders, ranging from middle ear diseases, such as otosclerosis and eustachian tube dysfunction, to inner ear and auditory nerve pathologies such as Ménière's disease and vestibular schwannoma. Nonauditory system disorders that can cause tinnitus include vascular anomalies, myoclonus, and intracranial hypertension. The Guideline Update Group (GUG) placed emphasis on the need for thorough clinical evaluation to identify these potentially treatable and sometimes serious disorders. However, patients with identifiable causative diagnoses other than sensorineural hearing loss are excluded from this guideline as they are excluded from nearly all randomized controlled trials of tinnitus management, making it impossible to generalize trial results to these patients. Nevertheless, clinicians should decide whether to apply the recommendations of this guideline to patients with these conditions on an individualized basis. The guideline also underscores the need to distinguish between subjective, objective, and pulsatile tinnitus to further direct patient evaluation and management. Comprehensive management of objective tinnitus and pulsatile tinnitus is not within the scope of this guideline. Pulsatile tinnitus is the perception of a rhythmic sound in the absence of an external source that may be pulse-synchronous, which is often but not always related to vascular causes, or pulse-asynchronous, which is typically associated with mechanical causes such as palatal or middle ear myoclonus.1 Further, the guideline does not apply to transient ear noise, which is the sudden perception of a tonal or ringing sound in 1 ear, lasting fewer than 5 minutes, that may be accompanied by a sense of hearing loss or aural fullness, as it does not typically require clinical management.2 The guideline also excludes patients with tinnitus related to complex auditory hallucinations or hallucinations related to psychotic or seizure disorders. This is an update to an evidence-based clinical guideline developed for the evaluation and management of tinnitus. This updated guideline provides clinicians with a logical framework to improve patient care and mitigate the personal and social effects of persistent, bothersome tinnitus. The first part of the guideline is focused on the clinical evaluation of patients with tinnitus, including the history, physical exam, and selection and timing of diagnostic testing and specialty referral to identify potential underlying treatable pathology and reduce the risk of self-harm. The remainder of the guideline is focused on the evaluation and treatment of patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus, with recommendations to evaluate and measure its effects as well as to determine the most appropriate interventions to improve symptoms and quality of life. ACTION STATEMENTS: The Guideline Update Group made strong recommendations for the following Key Action Statements (KAS): Clinicians should distinguish patients with bothersome tinnitus from patients with nonbothersome tinnitus (KAS 2). Clinicians should inquire about risks for self-harm in a patient with bothersome tinnitus (KAS 3). item.title: Roxadustat Treatment After PCI Among Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Quan W, Wang Y, Zhang M, Zhu T, Zhu J, Wang X, Zhu Z, Du R, Ding F, Ni J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Quan W, Wang Y, Zhang M, Zhu T, Zhu J, Wang X, Zhu Z, Du R, Ding F, Ni J, et al.
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.37953
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42853570



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preclinical studies suggest that stabilization of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) may attenuate reperfusion injury. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether oral roxadustat, a HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduced infarct size when administered after reperfusion among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 2, open-label, randomized clinical trial-Effect of Roxadustat in Acute Myocardial Infarction (ROXAMI)-enrolled adults with STEMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at a single tertiary medical center between April 1, 2021, and March 31, 2024, with follow-up through 1 year. INTERVENTIONS: Oral roxadustat (100 mg, 3 times per week for 2 weeks), initiated within 2 hours after primary PCI, or standard care alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was infarct size as a percentage of the left ventricle at 30 days measured by late gadolinium enhancement on [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FAPI-04 positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Prespecified secondary end points included major adverse cardiovascular events, myocardial injury markers, echocardiographic parameters, and myocardial fibroblast activation parameters on [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FAPI-04 PET and MRI. The primary efficacy analysis for infarct size was conducted in the modified intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: Among 158 randomized patients (mean [SD] age, 63.6 [11.0] years; 133 men [84.2%]; 79 randomized to each group), 148 (93.7%; 72 roxadustat and 76 control) had evaluable imaging for the primary outcome. For the primary end point, mean (SD) infarct size did not significantly differ between the roxadustat and control groups (23.3% [12.2%] vs 22.0% [12.2%]; mean difference, 1.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.7 to 5.3 percentage points; P = .51). Major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 3 of 79 patients (3.8%) in the roxadustat group and 7 of 79 (8.9%) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.11-1.63; P = .21). In multiplicity-unadjusted secondary analyses, adjusted between-group differences at 12 months were 2.9 percentage points (95% CI, 0.4-5.3 percentage points; P = .02) for the change in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean [SD]: roxadustat, 3.4% [0.9%] vs control, 0.5% [0.9%]) and -4.5 mL/m2 (95% CI, -8.9 to -0.1 mL/m2; P = .045) for left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (mean [SD]: roxadustat, 1.2 [1.6] mL/m2 vs control, 5.7 [1.6] mL/m2). The incidence of prespecified safety end points did not differ between the roxadustat and control groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of patients with STEMI, roxadustat administration after PCI did not significantly reduce infarct size at 30 days compared with control. Secondary ventricular remodeling findings were exploratory and require confirmation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04803864.

item.title: Bridging Clinical Observational Research and Data Standards in Head and Neck Cancer Care: Scoping Review and Mapping of Clinical Data Elements.

item.description:
Authors: Valerie IC, Aly F, Niknam Shirvan G, Alam FI, Johnston M, Kong BY, Findlay M, Holloway L, Kennedy G
Journal: JCO clinical cancer informatics | DOI: 10.1200/CCI-26-00177
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
PURPOSE: A scoping review and mapping of clinical data elements in observational studies were conducted to assess head and neck cancer (HNC) clinical data, alignment with existing observational oncology data standards, and the demonstrated opportunities for using these data standards in observational studies. METHODS: The scoping review was performed to systematically find and extract data elements from real-world studies emphasizing HNC treatment patterns. Text-embedding-assisted and manual mapping was performed to map data elements to their representations in HNC Ontology, Operational Ontology for Oncology, Minimal Common Oncology Data Elements, and the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model. Study characteristics, data elements and their mapping, and proportion of clinical domains represented were analyzed. Demonstrated opportunities for using standard data elements were reviewed based on the mapping results. RESULTS: A total of 98 observational studies were included. National databases were the most common data source (59.2%), and disease trajectory outcomes were the most frequently reported study end point (95.9%). Overall, 1,613 data elements were reported and classified into five domains: diagnosis (1.2%), health system (5.7%), tumor (27.2%), person (32.7%), and treatment (33.2%). Mapping coverage varied across domains, with 85%-100% coverage in diagnosis, 83.6%-95.2% in treatment, 85.3%-97.8% in tumor, 50.7%-89% in person, and 43.8%-81.2% in health system domains. Demonstrated opportunities for applying data standardization include facilitating geographical links to personal data elements, streamlining value derivation of longitudinally tracked data elements, and deriving complex treatment constructs. CONCLUSION: The existing data standards and associated terminology systems covered most of the clinical observational data elements, but gaps remain in structuring complex treatment factors that may affect patient outcomes. Resulting mapping offers generalizable representations across standards, laying the groundwork for further refinement through collaborative data element curation from local conventions under the guidance of data standard experts.

item.title: Determining the Causal Effect of Neurotrophic Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase Gene Fusions on Survival Prognosis for Adult Patients With Advanced Cancers.
item.dc:creator: Krebs E, Tamvada N, Weymann D, Lim HJ, Chia S, Ho C, Regier DA
item.description:
Authors: Krebs E, Tamvada N, Weymann D, Lim HJ, Chia S, Ho C, Regier DA
Journal: JCO precision oncology | DOI: 10.1200/PO-26-00281
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42842841



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Uncertainty about the prognostic significance of neurotrophic tropomyosin receptor kinase (NTRK) fusions complicates clinical decisions and interpretation of survival outcomes in oncology care. Drawing on the largest cohort of NTRK fusion-positive (NTRK+) patients, we establish the prognostic effect of NTRK fusions in adults with advanced cancers. METHODS: We used a large real-world clinicogenomic research database from the United States to emulate a pragmatic randomized trial that determines the causal effect of harboring an NTRK gene fusion (NTRK+) on survival prognosis for adult patients with advanced solid tumors. We 1:1 matched NTRK+ patients to patients with no identified NTRK genomic alterations (NTRK-) using a machine learning matching approach. Excluding patients who received TRK inhibitors, we conducted stratified matching within common tumor groups. We used Kaplan-Meier and Weibull regression survival analyses and estimated the difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST) over 1-, 2-, 3-, and 5-year study periods. RESULTS: We included 68,145 NTRK- patients for matching to 73 NTRK+ patients within seven tumor groups, including colorectal (n = 22), non-small cell lung (n = 13), sarcoma (n = 13), breast (n = 10), head and neck (n = 7), neuroendocrine (n = 4), and prostate (n = 4), and 14 NTRK+ patients representing eight other cancers. The difference in overall survival over 1 year was statistically significant using the Kaplan-Meier estimate (P = .008), Weibull regression (hazard ratio, 2.105 [95% CI, 1.207 to 3.673]), and RMST (-50 days [95% CI, -96 to -5]; P = .029). Differences were also statistically different at 2 years and 3 years. At 5 years, no survival differences were statistically significant. CONCLUSION: In this large real-world target trial emulation, NTRK gene fusions were associated with clinically meaningful reductions in overall survival among adults with advanced cancers not treated with TRK inhibitors. These findings clarify the prognostic role of NTRK fusions and inform clinical interpretation of outcomes in routine oncology.

item.title: Systemic therapy for metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma in the immunotherapy era: A critical review.
item.dc:creator: Wen W, Li J, Qu Y, Dong J, Huang J, Xuan Y, Wu P, Lee VHF
item.description:
Authors: Wen W, Li J, Qu Y, Dong J, Huang J, Xuan Y, Wu P, Lee VHF
Journal: Cancer treatment reviews | DOI: 10.1016/j.ctrv.2026.103214
Published: 2026-Sep-25
PMID: 42854616



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognosis of metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (mNPC) remains dismal despite recent advances of locoregional and systemic therapy. The incorporation of programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors into first-line chemotherapy has transformed the therapeutic landscape; however, optimal treatment strategies beyond initial chemo-immunotherapy remain undefined. METHODS: We conducted a critical review of prospective clinical trials, large retrospective studies, and translational research evaluating systemic therapies for mNPC in the immunotherapy era, with a focus on treatment sequencing and clinical decision-making. RESULTS: Multiple phase III trials have established gemcitabine-cisplatin combined with PD-1 blockade as the standard first-line treatment for recurrent or metastatic NPC, with mature follow-up now demonstrating durable overall survival benefits reaching up to 5 years. Subsequent-line treatment options include cytotoxic chemotherapy, anti-angiogenic agents, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and immunotherapy rechallenge strategies. Among these, VEGF-targeted combinations and EGFR/HER3-directed ADCs have demonstrated the most promising activity in PD-1-resistant disease, although toxicity profiles and durability of response vary across regimens. CONCLUSIONS: The treatment paradigm for mNPC is rapidly evolving beyond first-line chemo-immunotherapy. Emerging evidence supports biologically informed treatment selection incorporating angiogenesis inhibition, ADCs, and immune modulation. Prospective trials addressing optimal sequencing, predictive biomarkers, and integration of systemic and local therapies are urgently warranted.

item.title: Hypofractionated radiotherapy in head and neck cancer: current evidence and future directions, with a focus on laryngeal cancer.
item.dc:creator: Grossi C, Spahiu O, Riva G, Crupi A, Arduino PG, Pecorari G, Ricardi U, Iorio GC
item.description:
Authors: Grossi C, Spahiu O, Riva G, Crupi A, Arduino PG, Pecorari G, Ricardi U, Iorio GC
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1953291
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42852104



Abstract:
Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone in the management of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) across both definitive and multimodality treatment settings. While hypofractionated radiotherapy (HFRT) has become an established standard of care for several solid tumors, including prostate, breast, lung, and rectal cancers, its adoption in HNSCC has been more cautious owing to the complex anatomy of the head and neck region, the proximity of numerous critical organs at risk, and concerns regarding severe late toxicity. However, major advances in intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT), volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT), image guidance, adaptive radiotherapy, and radiobiological understanding have renewed interest in HFRT as a strategy to maintain oncological efficacy while reducing overall treatment time. Additional drivers include the need to optimize healthcare resource utilization, improve access to radiotherapy in low- and middle-income countries, and minimize hospital visits, as highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Recent prospective evidence has further strengthened the rationale for carefully selected hypofractionated approaches in HNSCC. In elderly and frail patients, the phase III ELAN-RT trial has also provided prospective evidence regarding a tailored hypofractionated approach for patients unable to undergo standard treatment. Among head and neck subsites, laryngeal cancer-particularly early-stage glottic carcinoma-represents the most mature clinical model for HFRT and therefore constitutes the principal focus of this review, while evidence from other HNSCC subsites is examined to assess the broader applicability of hypofractionated treatment strategies. This review critically summarizes the radiobiological rationale, current clinical evidence, technological advances, and ongoing challenges surrounding radical HFRT in HNSCC, with particular emphasis on laryngeal cancer, and discusses future directions for its broader implementation in clinical practice.

item.title: TET1 loss promotes malignant phenotypes in HeLa cells and is associated with altered PTEN-PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling.
item.dc:creator: Liu Y, Liu L, Wang L, Ren J, Meng F, Chen M, Yao X, Zou P, Wu J, Zhou X, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Liu Y, Liu L, Wang L, Ren J, Meng F, Chen M, Yao X, Zou P, Wu J, Zhou X, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963427
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42851704



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the biological significance of ten-eleven translocation 1 (TET1) in cervical cancer and its association with PTEN-PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. METHODS: Publicly available bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets were analyzed, with histology-restricted analyses focused on cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). TET1 immunoreactivity was assessed in five paired cervical adenocarcinoma and adjacent non-neoplastic tissues using nuclear H-scores. TET1 loss of function was modeled in HeLa cells by shRNA-mediated knockdown, with Bobcat339 used as a complementary TET-family inhibitor. Cellular metabolic activity, clonogenicity, cell-cycle distribution, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were evaluated using CCK-8, colony-formation, flow-cytometric, wound-healing, and Transwell assays. Protein expression and phosphorylation were examined by western blotting. RESULTS: SCC-restricted bulk analyses consistently showed lower TET1 expression in cervical SCC than in normal cervical tissues. In TCGA-CESC SCC, TET1 expression was not significantly associated with PTEN expression or the PI3K-AKT-mTOR transcriptional score after multiple-testing correction, whereas an inverse association with the apoptosis score remained significant. Patient-level pseudobulk analysis of 12 SCC cases likewise identified no pathway association that remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. In five paired cervical adenocarcinoma cases, TET1 nuclear H-scores were lower in all tumor samples than in their matched adjacent tissues, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (exact P = 0.0625). In HeLa cells, TET1 depletion increased cellular metabolic activity and clonogenicity, altered cell-cycle distribution, reduced apoptosis, and enhanced migration and invasion. These changes were accompanied by reduced PTEN expression and increased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and mTOR. CONCLUSION: Reduced TET1 expression was observed in SCC-restricted public cohorts, while TET1 depletion promoted malignant phenotypes in HeLa cells. The accompanying changes in PTEN expression and PI3K/AKT/mTOR phosphorylation identify a candidate signaling association that warrants validation through rescue experiments and locus-specific epigenetic studies.

item.title: Quercetin selectively targets gingival squamous cell carcinoma through apoptosis induction, autophagy suppression, DNA damage, and chemosensitization.
item.dc:creator: Semlali A, Baroudi S, Nimbarte VD, Sonak SS, Issa H, Cornillaut J, Almutairi MH, Rouabhia M
item.description:
Authors: Semlali A, Baroudi S, Nimbarte VD, Sonak SS, Issa H, Cornillaut J, Almutairi MH, Rouabhia M
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1890978
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42851387



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major clinical challenge due to high recurrence rates, chemotherapy resistance, and severe treatment-related toxicity. Although quercetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, has demonstrated anti-cancer properties, its selective activity and molecular mechanisms in distinct OSCC subtypes remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: In this study, we investigated the anti-tumor effects of quercetin in human gingival squamous cell carcinoma (Ca9-22), tongue carcinoma (SCC-9 and CAL-27), and non-malignant oral epithelial (GMSM-K) cells. RESULTS: Quercetin (0-100 µM) selectively reduced the viability, proliferation, and clonogenic potential of gingival carcinoma cells while exerting limited cytotoxicity toward non-malignant oral epithelial cells, suggesting a favorable therapeutic index. Mechanistically, quercetin induced apoptosis through modulation of intrinsic and extrinsic apoptotic pathways, suppressed autophagy, reduced oxidative stress, promoted DNA damage, and inhibited migratory and metastatic potential. Transcriptomic profiling identified several apoptosis-related genes modulated by quercetin, including CASP9 and BIRC3, whose elevated expression was associated with improved overall survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma datasets. In addition, quercetin enhanced the anti-proliferative effects of cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil, supporting its potential role as a chemosensitizing agent in OSCC therapy. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations further demonstrated stable interactions between quercetin and apoptosis- and DNA damage-related proteins, including CASP9, H2AX, and BIRC3. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings identify quercetin as a selective multi-target anti-cancer compound capable of modulating apoptosis, autophagy, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and metastatic pathways in gingival squamous cell carcinoma. These data support the translational potential of quercetin as a complementary strategy to enhance chemotherapy efficacy in oral cancer.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of acupuncture for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Lin Z, Shi H, Tao Y, Liu H, Chen L, Zhao J, Liu S
item.description:
Authors: Lin Z, Shi H, Tao Y, Liu H, Chen L, Zhao J, Liu S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1919320
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42851298



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acupuncture has been used as an adjunctive supportive intervention for various cancer-related symptoms. However, its efficacy and safety for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma have not been systematically evaluated. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The outcomes were post-treatment Water Swallowing Test (WST) scores, the proportion of patients achieving a favorable swallowing status, the clinical effective rate, videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) outcomes, and Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) scores. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, Wanfang Database, and VIP Database were searched from inception to March 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software. RESULTS: Twelve randomized controlled trials including 863 patients were analyzed. Acupuncture reduced post-treatment WST scores compared with control interventions (MD = -0.78, 95% CI: -1.04 to -0.51). The clinical effective rate was also higher in the acupuncture group (RR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.08 to 1.27). Moreover, acupuncture improved VFSS outcomes (SMD = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.46 to 1.05), reduced SSA scores (MD = -7.65, 95% CI: -12.30 to -3.01), and improved quality of life and nutritional indicators. Safety reporting was limited, precluding definitive conclusions regarding the safety of acupuncture in this population. CONCLUSION: Acupuncture may have a potential adjunctive role in improving swallowing function, swallowing-related quality of life, and nutritional indicators in patients with dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma. However, the evidence remains limited by small sample sizes, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity across outcomes. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings and further clarify the clinical role of acupuncture. item.title: Associations of Orthognathic Surgery With Body Image Perception, Facial Appearance, and Quality of Life.
item.dc:creator: Benato LS, Molinari R, Clazer JPS, Fanderuff M, Sebastiani AM, Scariot R

Published: 2026-Sep-23

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) affects approximately 15% of individuals seeking orthognathic surgery and may compromise postoperative satisfaction. PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between orthognathic surgery and changes in body image dissatisfaction, facial appearance perception, and oral health-related quality of life, and the correlations among these outcomes. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, AND SAMPLE: Prospective cohort study at the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Service, Federal University of Paraná, Brazil, of subjects aged 18 years or older with skeletal Class II or Class III malocclusion scheduled for orthognathic surgery between 2022 and 2024. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: Surgical status (preoperative [T0] and 6 months postoperative [T1]). MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLES: Primary outcomes: body image dissatisfaction, measured by the Body Dysmorphic Disorder Examination (BDDE; range 0 to 168, higher scores indicating greater dissatisfaction), and possible BDD status (BDDE score > 66). SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Psychosocial Impact of Facial Aesthetics Scale (EPAF; range 0 to 88) and Oral Health Impact Profile short form (OHIP-14; range 0 to 56). COVARIATES: Age, biological sex at birth (male/female), self-reported race, and skeletal classification (Class II vs Class III). DATA ANALYSES: Wilcoxon signed-rank test, McNemar's test, and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rho); statistical significance at P < .05. RESULTS: Of 50 subjects assessed, 45 (23 [51%] female; median age 27 years, interquartile range [IQR] = 12) were included. Possible BDD was identified in 5 subjects (11%) at T0 and 2 (4%) at T1 (P = .3). The median BDDE score decreased from 28 (IQR = 42.5) to 21 (IQR = 18.5), EPAF from 9 (IQR = 12) to 4 (IQR = 6), and OHIP-14 from 12 (IQR = 13.5) to 3 (IQR = 8.5) (all P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Orthognathic surgery was associated with statistically significant improvements in body image dissatisfaction, facial appearance perception, and oral health-related quality of life, and with fewer subjects screening positive for possible BDD.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The high recurrence rate following definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a paramount clinical challenge. However, there is currently a lack of research to explore the different effects of inflammation-related indicators on early recurrence (ER) and late recurrence (LR). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 905 locally advanced ESCC patients. Six machine learning algorithms were used for consensus feature selection, followed by multivariate Cox regression to identify independent prognostic factors for ER and LR. A prognostic nomogram was developed, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) quantified survival differences, guiding follow-up strategies. RESULTS: Machine learning combined with Cox analysis identified RT dose, tumor thickness, and N stage as independent risk factors for ER, while concurrent chemotherapy, N stage, pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR) were identified for LR. Risk models effectively stratified patients into high-, moderate-, and low-risk groups with significantly distinct PFS and OS, and high-risk groups were enriched with adverse features including elevated N stage, PAR, PIV, and tumor burden. The developed nomogram demonstrated good calibration, discriminative ability (with 5-year OS and PFS AUC values of 0.738 and 0.771), and provided higher net clinical benefit than single variables. The C-index of the model was 0.652 and 0.677 for OS and PFS. Based on RMST analysis revealing a significant survival gradient across risk subgroups (5-year OS-RMST: 21.0 vs. 32.5 vs. 44.7 months for high-, moderate-, and low-risk groups, respectively), a risk-stratified follow-up strategy was developed, recommending intensive (every 1-3 months), step-down, and annual surveillance schedules for high-, moderate-, and low-risk patients. CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a prognostic nomogram based on inflammatory indicators that can effectively quantify risks and stratify them. Moreover, we formulated a novel risk-adaptive follow-up strategy framework based on RMST, providing potential decision-making tools for the individualized and precise management of ESCC. However, this strategy remains hypothesis-generating and requires external prospective validation before widespread clinical adoption.

Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1574103
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42846024



Abstract:
Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is associated with limited therapeutic options and poor clinical prognosis. The Octamer nucleotide--binding transcription factor (NONO), which lacks the POU domain, is implicated in nearly every aspect of gene regulation. It participates in various biological processes including cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and DNA damage repair. In this study, we report elevated expression of the NONO gene in LUSC as identified through tumor databases. Our biological function experiments confirmed that NONO promotes the proliferation of LUSC cells by inhibiting apoptosis and enhances the tumor cells' capabilities for invasion and metastasis. Through the mediation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, NONO regulates downstream molecules such as FOXO1 and GSK3β, which are related to cell proliferation and apoptosis. It participates in the regulation of LUSC cell proliferation, invasion and metastasis, and can serve as a potential clinical target for LUSC, providing ideas for exploring new treatment methods.

item.title: Preoperative risk stratification for pulmonary complications after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Lv H, Wang M, Zhu M, Lu T, Ma Y, Han R
item.description:
Authors: Lv H, Wang M, Zhu M, Lu T, Ma Y, Han R
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1911374
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42857285



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are a major cause of morbidity among patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) undergoing esophagectomy. Risk stratification is crucial for patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy (NAT), as their perioperative course differs. We aimed to identify preoperatively available factors associated with PPCs after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy and to develop a practical model for preoperative risk stratification. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive adults with locally advanced ESCC who underwent NAT [chemotherapy (NCT) or immunochemotherapy (NICT)] followed by curative-intent esophagectomy (2023-2024). PPCs were defined a priori and retrospectively ascertained through standardized chart review. The prediction time point was immediately before esophagectomy, and model development was restricted to preoperatively available variables. Five predictors were entered simultaneously into a multivariable logistic regression model. Performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis, with internal validation using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. RESULTS: Among 232 eligible patients, 69 (29.7%) experienced PPCs. In the final model, smoking history was associated with higher odds of PPCs, whereas hypertension, NICT versus NCT, preoperative nebulization, and preoperative respiratory exercise were associated with lower odds. The model showed acceptable discrimination [apparent Area Under the Curve (AUC), 0.783; optimism-corrected AUC, 0.764] and acceptable calibration after bootstrap internal validation. Decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. The model was presented as a nomogram for individualized preoperative risk estimation. CONCLUSIONS: A model based on five preoperatively available variables showed acceptable performance for PPC risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy in locally advanced ESCC. The nomogram may support individualized preoperative risk estimation, but external validation and prospective impact assessment are required before clinical implementation.

item.title: The CGRP-nociceptor axis in cancer: tumor-specific programs of immune evasion, stromal remodeling, and tumor growth.
item.dc:creator: Hua Y, Liu Y, Wang B, Liu Y, Tian X, Liu F, Tian Q, Yin F
item.description:
Authors: Hua Y, Liu Y, Wang B, Liu Y, Tian X, Liu F, Tian Q, Yin F
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968354
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42840415



Abstract:
Cancer neuroscience has established that peripheral nerves can shape tumor growth and antitumor immunity, although the underlying mechanisms vary across malignancies. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), released mainly by peptidergic nociceptors and sensed through the CALCRL/RAMP1 receptor complex, is emerging as a recurrent mediator of tumor-nerve communication. This review synthesizes current evidence for CGRP signaling across tumor types. In melanoma and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), CGRP can directly suppress tumor-infiltrating T cell activity. In lung adenocarcinoma, it acts through a macrophage-fibroblast relay that limits tertiary lymphoid structure assembly. In medullary thyroid cancer, tumor-associated CGRP is linked to abnormal dendritic cell development. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, nociceptor-derived CGRP participates in a reciprocal interaction with cancer-associated fibroblasts that lowers IL-15 and suppresses natural killer cells. Additional studies identify tumor-intrinsic outputs, including gastric tumor growth, CGRP-dependent cytoprotective autophagy in oral cancer, and RAMP1-dependent growth in gastrointestinal cancer models. Liver data currently support a role in fibrogenesis, while the relevance of this pathway to hepatocellular carcinoma remains unresolved. Together, these findings support a shared nociceptor-CGRP signaling system with tumor-specific cellular outputs. CGRP-pathway drugs and nociceptor-directed interventions therefore warrant tumor-specific translational studies, although anticancer efficacy remains predominantly preclinical.
